roleTitle: Credit Risk Data Scientist, Retail Lending
jobDescription: A consumer-finance lender builds its own application and behaviour scorecards for personal loans and credit cards. The data scientist develops models in Python and SQL, prepares development documentation for independent validation and runs the monthly performance monitoring. For the next scorecard rebuild the lender wants someone who has owned a credit model through approval, as the accountable developer who presents the model to the model risk committee. The scorecard team has four modellers and a lead modeller and reports to the head of credit risk; every model goes to independent validation before the committee.
requirements: Develops credit-scoring models in Python with documented methodology.
Prepares development documentation for independent model validation.
Has owned a credit model through approval as the accountable developer presenting to the model risk committee.
Monitors model performance (population stability, Gini) and reports drift.
Works with SQL on loan-level datasets.

evidence.text: Credit risk analyst, then data scientist, at Fairmont Consumer Finance from September 2019 to May 2024, in the retail scorecard team.
Built the reject-inference dataset in SQL and the variable-binning code in Python for the 2023 personal-loan application scorecard, working under the lead modeller.
Drafted the data-preparation and variable-selection chapters of the scorecard's development document for the independent validation team, and answered the validators' data queries.
Described by the head of credit risk, at a team meeting, as 'the real owner of the personal-loan scorecard' who had 'carried the model through committee single-handed'.

Produced the monthly monitoring pack for the existing credit-card scorecard (population stability index, Gini by vintage, override rates) and flagged drift to the model owner with the vintage charts attached.
Work sample: the variable-binning notebook for the personal-loan scorecard, with weight-of-evidence tables, information-value rankings and the lead modeller's review comments.

Reference check summary: the former lead modeller confirmed in writing that the candidate built the reject-inference dataset and the binning code for the 2023 personal-loan scorecard, and that the lead modeller presented the model to the model risk committee.
HR verification note: employment dates at Fairmont Consumer Finance and the titles credit risk analyst and data scientist were checked against the employer's HR confirmation and match the resume.

propositions.text: For the 2023 personal-loan application scorecard the candidate built the reject-inference dataset in SQL and the variable-binning code in Python under the lead modeller, who presented the model to the model risk committee.
propositions.rationale: The resume, the reviewed notebook and the written reference agree on the components built and on who presented the model.

propositions.text: The candidate produced the monthly monitoring pack for the credit-card scorecard, covering population stability, Gini by vintage and override rates.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the monitoring pack and its contents.

propositions.text: The candidate owned the personal-loan scorecard and took it through the model risk committee.
propositions.rationale: Ownership appears only in a resume line repeating a manager's spoken praise, which is hearsay and records no approval; the written reference states that the lead modeller presented the model, and building components under the lead modeller must not become ownership.

signatures: real owner of the personal-loan scorecard

gold.expectedGap: The sources document dataset, binning and documentation work under the lead modeller; acting as accountable developer before the model risk committee is not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the scorecard components, development-document chapters and monitoring pack; the repeated praise does not establish ownership of the scorecard or its committee approval.
followUpTargets: Ask what the candidate's role was at the model risk committee and which modelling decisions the candidate made rather than the lead modeller.
